newsitem.title: USA: House panel OKs $13 bln energy, lands spending bill.
newsitem.headline: House panel OKs $13 bln energy, lands spending bill.

text.p: The U.S. House appropriations committee Thursday passed a $13 billion spending bill for energy and lands programs for the 1998 fiscal year.

The spending level was $100 million less than the Clinton administration requested and $500 million less than was approved for 1997, but 1997 funding included more than $600 million in emergency spending.
The bill included approval for 3.8 billion board feet of timber sales from federal forests, which are expected to raise about $750 million in the 1998 fiscal year, which begins October 1.
The bill also included a plan to sell $209 million worth of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to cover the costs of operating the nation's emergency stock pile.

However, the committee rejected an amendment to sell an additional $89 million of oil to help keep the National Endowment for the Arts alive. The committee also defeated an amendment to provide $65 million to pay off a company not to develop a gold mine on the edge of Yellowstone National Park and $250 million to trade forest lands in California to protect the Headwaters old growth forest from development.
The bill now goes to the full House, where it is expected to be debated in July.
